neighbours.label: nouns for a bundle of things gathered together (bunch, cluster, bouquet, bundle)
fire: She bought a small bunch of radishes at the Saturday market.
Hang a bunch of lavender upside down in the hallway to dry it.
The groom carried a bouquet of white roses down the aisle.
The vine produced heavy clusters of purple grapes this autumn.
He tied a bundle of sticks together with a length of string.
A bunch of keys jangled from the caretaker's belt.
The shrub flowers in dense clusters of tiny yellow blossoms.
Pick a bouquet of wildflowers from the meadow for the table.
quiet: She bought a small basket of radishes at the Saturday market.
Hang a pot of lavender by the window in the hallway to dry it.
The groom carried a single white rose down the aisle.
The vine produced heavy crops of purple grapes this autumn.
He tied a piece of wood to the fence with a length of string.
A set of tools jangled from the caretaker's belt.
The shrub flowers in early spring with tiny yellow blossoms.
Pick a jar of honey from the shelf for the table.

notes: Card: ' bunch' x7, ' clusters' x3, ' bouquet' x3, Russian пучков, Korean 묶음 (bundle), racemes. Distinction: a gathered bundle vs a container or single item.
